newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle up sharply on fund demand.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle up sharply on fund demand.

text.p: CME live cattle futures ran up to five-week highs in active trade as fund demand touched off buy stops, traders said.
December live cattle ran up to 67.775 cents per lb, up 1.050 cents, at 1044 CST. Other months were up 0.775 to 0.225 cents.
Support from fundamentals boosted futures and fund demand developed on a technical breakout to the upside. Buy stops were hit above a trend line and last week's high, they said.
Fundamental demand stemmed from very current feedlot conditions, traders said. Some cattle meant for late November and December marketings have been sold ahead of schedule.

The market was pressured last week by expectations for increased fed cattle supplies and lower prices in December. But the active feedlot movement has taken away much of that concern, especially with the large discount that futures already hold to cash on seasonal concerns, they added.

Cash cattle sold at $72.00 per cwt in central and southern Plains direct feedlot trade last week, and at $73.00 in the upper Midwest. The prices were well above CME December futures which at 1057 CST were trading 0.975 cent higher at 67.700 cent a lb.
E.D.& F. Man, Cargill Investor Services, Dean Witter, Refco and R.J. O'Brien bought, pit sources added. Refco also spread long February/short December, sources said.

Feeder cattle futures followed the lead of live cattle with March up sharply to a new contract high of 67.450 cents a lb, up 1.150 cents. Other months were up 1.175 to 0.200 cent with January up most at 68.050 cents.

Good demand for replacement feeders and a higher CME Feeder Cattle Index added to overall strength and offset any resistance from higher corn futures. Active fed cattle sales are prompting demand for replacement feeders, traders said.
The latest CME index was up $0.37 at $63.85 per cwt, the highest level since October 3.
